en: O Agni, you have made me the bearer of the powerful Soma, so that I may sacrifice at the assembly;
shining toward the gods, I harness the pressing-stone—O Agni, take pleasure in my body.
We have performed the sacrifice facing forward; let the song increase. With fuel and with reverence, they honor Agni.
The wise have ordained the sacrificial rites for the poets of heaven; they have sought a path for the one who is skillful and strong.

The sage, pure in will, has established joy; by his very birth, he is the close kinsman of heaven and earth. The gods found the beautiful Agni within the waters, performing their work among the sisters.
The seven mighty rivers have magnified the fortunate one; he was born white, yet red in his greatness.
As if to a newborn infant, the divine horses hastened toward him; the gods marveled at Agni at his birth.
With his bright limbs he has stretched across the mid-air, purifying his will through the purifiers of the seers.
Clothed in radiance, encompassing the life-span of the waters, he measures out vast and perfect glories.

He has gone to the unceasing, inviolable, mighty daughters of heaven, who are clothed in splendor yet remain unadorned. There, the ancient ones, though youthful and of common origin, have borne a single germ within their seven voices.
His compact masses, assuming every form, are spread out in the womb of clarified butter, in the flow of honeyed streams.
Here stand the swelling milch-cows; the two great, united Mothers of the wondrous one are present.
O Son of Strength, being borne along, you have shone forth, putting on brilliant and impetuous forms.
The streams of honeyed ghee drip down where the Bull has grown strong through poetic wisdom.
By his very birth he found the udder even of his father; he released its streams and poured forth its milky flows.
Moving in secret with his auspicious friends, the great ones of heaven, he was not hidden away.
He bore the embryo of the father and the progenitor; alone he sucked many teeming [streams]. Both wives, the co-spouses and kinswomen, belong to this pure bull; protect them both, O human one.
In the wide, unconfined space, the great one grew; for the glorious waters have gathered together in abundance around Agni.
In the womb of Order, the domestic lord Agni lay within the lap of his sisters, the kindred ones.
Like a horse bearing the prize in the encounter of the great waters, he—whose light is straight—is eager to be beheld by his son.
He who as father begat the ruddy cows, Agni, the most manly germ of the waters, the youthful one, has arisen.
The most beautiful germ of the waters, the plants have brought forth from the woods—him who is auspicious and multiform.
Even the gods, having come together in spirit, have honored him, the most praiseworthy and powerful one, at his birth.
Mighty rays, bright as lightnings, attend Agni, whose luster is straight and pure.
Like one hidden in a cave, you dwell within your own assembly; in the boundless expanse, they milk the nectar of immortality.
I praise you with oblations as a sacrificer; desiring your friendship and favor, I praise you.
Together with the gods, grant protection to the singer, and guard us with your domestic powers.

O Agni, our leaders, well-guided by you, shall possess all riches; impelled by glorious vigor, may we overcome the godless who attack us in battle. O Agni, you became the banner of the gods, the delightful one, knowing all poetic wisdoms.
As the domestic friend, you have settled the mortals; as the charioteer, you have gone forth accomplishing the gods' work.
The immortal king has sat down in the dwelling of mortals, fulfilling the sacrificial assemblies.
With his face anointed with ghee, Agni has shone far and wide, knowing all secret wisdoms.
Come to us with your auspicious friendships, O Great One, with your great protections, you who hasten to help.
Bestow upon us abundant wealth that crosses over all difficulties, and grant us a glorious portion accompanied by fair speech.
These ancient births of yours, O Agni, and these new ones, I have proclaimed to you, the Primordial One.
These great libations have been prepared for the Bull; from birth to birth, Jātavedas has been established.
From birth to birth, Jātavedas, established as the eternal one, is kindled by the Viśvāmitras. May we abide in the favor of that worshipful one, and in his auspicious goodwill.
O powerful one, O wise one, bestowing gifts, place this sacrifice of ours among the gods. O Hotṛ, Agni, grant us abundant nourishment; through sacrifice, win for us great wealth.
O Agni, bestow upon the invoker Iḷā—the gift of cattle, most wondrous and eternal.
May there be to us a son, a spreading progeny; O Agni, may that benevolence of yours be with us.
For Vaiśvānara Agni, who increases the cosmic order (*ṛta*), we fashion our prayer like purified clarified butter.
Twofold—both as the invoker for men and as the priest—the worshippers fashion him with their inspired thought, just as a craftsman fashions a chariot with an axe.
By his very birth, he illumined both heaven and earth; he became the praiseworthy son of his two parents.

Agni, the bearer of oblations, ageless and well-established, the invincible guest of the people, rich in radiance—by the power of their skillful will, within the cosmic order, the gods generated Agni through their insights.

Desiring to win the prize, I address the great lord who shines with his radiant light, like one seeking booty. Desiring to win, we choose from the gracious one that desirable, bold, and praiseworthy strength— the gift of the Bhr̥gus, the eager one, possessed of the wisdom of a seer, Agni, ruling with celestial splendor.

For the sake of bliss, men who have spread the sacrificial grass here have placed Agni at their head— him whose fame is for booty, the one of beautiful luster belonging to all the gods, the Rudra of sacrifices, the fulfiller of desires, and the director of labors. O Purifier, O Hotṛ, for around your dwelling at the sacrifices, the men who have spread the sacrificial grass [gather].
O Agni, those seeking worship and kinship wait upon you; bestow wealth upon them.
At his birth, he filled the two worlds, the great heaven, when the skillful ones sustained him. He, the seer, is led around for the sacrifice like a steed set forth to win the prize.
Worship him who accepts the oblation; honor the domestic Jātavedas, the performer of the fair sacrifice.
Agni, the charioteer of the lofty cosmic order (*ṛta*), the all-seeing, has become the domestic priest of the gods.
The three kindling-sticks of the mighty Agni, who encompasses the world, have purified the *uśij*—those who are free from death.
Of these, they assigned one to mortals for enjoyment; two went toward their kin.
The human nourishments have fashioned him, the seer of the tribes and lord of the people, like an axe for the sake of sharpness.
He goes to the heights and the depths, busily active; he has established his germ within these worlds.
Having been born, he stirs within the bellies, roaring like a lion among the variegated [beasts],
the bull Vaiśvānara, immortal and broad-chested, distributing goods and treasures to the donor.
Vaiśvānara has ascended to the firmament, to the back of heaven, as of old, being celebrated by those of good thoughts.
Like before, generating wealth for all people, he, the watchful one, goes around the common racecourse.
Him, the observer of *ṛta*, the worshipful sage worthy of praise, whom Mātariśvan established as a dweller in heaven—
him, Agni, with his bright path and golden hair, the radiant one, we implore for new prosperity.
Like the pure one on his course, impetuous, beholding the light of heaven, the banner of the sky stationed in the luminous realm,
awakening at dawn— Agni, the head of heaven, the unassailable, the possessor of strength, him we implore with great reverence.
The delightful invoker, pure, free from duplicity, the domestic friend, worthy of praise, the one who watches over all people.
Like a wondrous chariot, beautiful to behold and established by Manu, we ever seek him for the sake of wealth.
To Vaiśvānara of the broad expanse, the inspired singers offer their treasures so that he may go upon his foundations.
For Agni, the immortal, serves the gods; thus he has not violated the eternal laws.
The wondrous messenger moves between the two worlds, the Hotṛ seated as the domestic priest of man.
Agni, enriched by prayer and impelled by the gods, adorns his vast dwelling day by day.
The wise ones magnify Agni with their thoughts—him who is the banner of sacrifices and the winner of wealth in the assembly.
In whom the singers have placed their sacred works, in him the sacrificer hopes for blessings.

The father of sacrifices, the lord of the wise, Agni, the measure and the path of the priests, has entered the two worlds of manifold form; the sage, beloved by many, is glorified through his manifestations.

The gods have established here Agni, who is like the moon, whose chariot is radiant, whose laws are golden, the Vaiśvānara seated within the waters, the finder of heaven; the one who plunges forward, the swift, encompassed by powers, the impetuous and glorious one.
Agni, together with the gods and the human race, weaves the sacrifice—multiform through inspired thought—with his own body.
The charioteer moves within with successful prayers, the active master of the house, the dispeller of curses.
O Agni, be wakeful for our long life and good progeny; swell us with vigor and shine upon us with nourishment.
Quicken our vital powers, O watchful one; you are the eager messenger of the gods and the wise inspirer of prayers.

The men ever praise the Lord of the People, the mighty Guest, the director of thoughts and the one who desires the prayers of the priests—Jātavedas, the conscious one of the sacrifices—with homage and with incitements for his increase.
Radiant, a god, a source of joy, Agni has encompassed the dwellings with his power; he whose chariot is well-favored.
May we, in this dwelling, honor with our well-fashioned hymns the sacred vows of him who nourishes many.
O Vaiśvānara, I long for your manifestations, by which you, O far-seeing one, became the finder of light.
O Agni, as soon as you were born, you filled the worlds and the two realms; you encompass all these things by your own self.
From the wondrous deeds of Vaiśvānara, the solitary sage has brought forth a great song through his skillful work.
Exalting both his parents, Heaven and Earth, who possess abundant seed, Agni was born. With every kindling-stick, be well-disposed toward us; with every flame, grant us the favor of wealth.
O God, bring the gods here for the sacrifice; as a friend, with a gracious mind, worship your friends, O Agni.
He whom the gods—Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—sacrifice to thrice a day, day after day;
O Tanūnapāt, make this our sacrifice sweet, you who have your source in ghee and are served by us.

The prayer, containing all desirable things, goes forth to worship the Hotṛ first for the sake of the oblation; let us honor the Bull with salutations, so that he, the most excellent sacrificer, being impelled, may sacrifice to the gods.
Upright has your path been made at the sacrifice; upright have the flames ascended through the regions.
Or at the navel of heaven the Hotṛ has sat down; we spread the sacrificial grass, wide-reaching for the gods.
Choosing in their minds the seven priestly offices, inciting all by means of the Truth (Ṛta), they come toward this sacrifice in many ways—those adorned with men, born at the assemblies.
The two Dawns, being praised, draw near; smiling, they appear with bodies of different forms, so that Mitra, Varuṇa, and Indra with the Maruts may be pleased by our great deeds.
I honor the two divine Hotṛ-priests first; the seven nourishers feast according to their own nature.
Proclaiming the *ṛta*, they speak only of the *ṛta* to you, as guardians of the vow, meditating upon the sacred law.
May Bhāratī, in harmony with the Bhāratīs; Iḷā with the gods; and Agni with men;
and Sarasvatī with the followers of Sarasvant—may these three goddesses sit here upon this sacred grass (*barhis*).

O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, being gracious, release for us that which is most excellent and nourishing, from which is born a hero—skillful in action, highly dexterous, one who sets the pressing-stones in motion, and a lover of the gods.
O Lord of the Forest, release [the oblation] toward the gods; let Agni, the immolator, prepare the offering.
Let him, the most truthful Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice, for he knows the generations of the gods. Come hither, O Agni, being well-kindled, on the same chariot with Indra and the swift gods.
Let Aditi, the mother of noble sons, sit upon our sacrificial grass. With the cry of Svāhā, let the immortal gods rejoice.

Agni has woken up, facing the dawns, the wise seer who observes the tracks of the sages. With broad radiance, kindled by those seeking the gods, the bearer of oblations has thrown open the doors of darkness.
Agni has waxed mighty through the praises and songs of the worshippers, O worshipful one, and through their hymns of praise.
Delighting in the many manifestations of *ṛta*, the messenger has shone forth today at the dawning of the dawn.
Agni has been established among the human tribes, the offspring of the waters, fulfilling the covenant as Mitra.
Desirable and worthy of sacrifice, he has taken his place upon the high ridge; the inspired sage has become the one who receives the oblations of the people.
Agni becomes Mitra when he is kindled; Mitra is the Hotṛ, Varuṇa is Jātavedas.
Mitra is the vigorous Adhvaryu, the friend of the household; Mitra belongs to the rivers as well as to the mountains.
He guards the beloved summit of the earth, the footstep of the bird; he guards the path of the sacrificer and the course of the sun.
Agni guards the seven-headed one in his navel; the lofty one guards the delight of the gods.
The Ribhu has fashioned for himself a praiseworthy and beautiful name, he, the god who knows all ways.
He clothes himself in the skin of the grain; Agni watches over that footstep of his, never failing.
Agni has taken his place at the ghee-rich womb, wide-striding, desiring it as he is desired;
shining, pure, lofty, and purifying, he makes his two mothers ever new again and again.
As soon as born, he grew by means of the plants when they, the self-sprouting ones, nourish him with ghee.
Like waters gliding down a slope, Agni, beautifying himself, has spread wide in the lap of his parents.
Praised with kindled fuel, the mighty one has shone forth from the height of heaven, at the navel of the earth.
Agni is Mitra, worthy of praise; as Mātariśvan, the messenger, he shall carry the gods here for the sacrifice.

The lofty Agni, becoming the highest of the luminous realms, propped up the firmament with his fuel when Mātariśvan kindled him from among the Bhr̥gus as the carrier of oblations, though he was hidden in secret. O Agni, [bring] Iḷā...
O singers, being urged by your thoughts, you who seek the gods lead [the ladle] toward the gods.
Carrying the sacrificial oblation, the vigorous, butter-dripping ladle goes forward to the east, bringing the offering for Agni.
Being born, you filled the two worlds, O most worshipful one; indeed, you have surpassed them.
Even from heaven and from the earth, O Agni, let your seven-tongued carriers speed forth by your greatness.
Heaven and earth, and the worshipful gods, establish you as the Hotṛ priest for the household.
When the human clans, seeking the gods and bearing offerings, praise your bright radiance.
The great one is seated firmly in his dwelling, encompassing the two exalted worlds, the heaven and earth, as he is desired.
The two co-wives, unaging and inviolable, the two milch-cows of the wide-striding one, yield their abundance together.
O Agni, the ordinances of you, the great one, are mighty; by your will you have extended across the two worlds, heaven and earth.
At your birth you became the messenger; you, O Bull, are the leader of the peoples.
Or rather, with the two long-maned, ruddy steeds that drip with ghee, yoke them to the pole of the *ṛta*.
Then, O God, bring hither all the gods; O Jātavedas, make our sacrifice well-performed.
Even from heaven your lights shine forth; O Dawn, as you beam brightly, you outshine many others.
O Agni, when you burn eagerly among the woods, the gods marvel at the waters of the joyous Hotṛ.
Whether they are the gods who rejoice in the wide mid-air, or those who dwell in the luminous realm of heaven—
RV_03.006.08.2 Those who are helpers, worthy of invocation and worship, who have extended themselves—O Agni, the horses that draw the chariot.
RV_03.006.09.1 Come hither with these, O Agni, on one chariot or on various chariots, for your horses are powerful.
Bring the thirty-three gods accompanied by their wives according to our desire; rejoice yourself.
He is the Hotṛ priest for whom even the two vast worlds, Heaven and Earth, praise every sacrifice for its increase.
They stand facing forward at the well-established rite, like two pure ones, true to the Eternal Law (ṛta) for him who is born of the Eternal Law.
O Agni, [bestow] Iḷā...

Those who have ascended from the nourishment of the white-backed one have entered the two parents and the seven voices. The two parents, dwelling around, move together; they hasten forward to bestow long life. The milch-cows dwelling in heaven are the mares of the bull; he has mounted the goddesses who carry the honeyed [soma].
In the seat of *ṛta*, the cow moves along her path alone around you as you rest there.
The wise husband, the finder of riches among treasures, has mounted them so that they become well-governed.
He of the dark-blue back, with his many faces, has caused them to dwell forth from the drink of the *atasa* plant.
The mighty, ageless, and strengthening waters carry him who is being established;
he, shining with his limbs in his dwelling place, has entered the two worlds as if they were one.
They know the favor of the ruddy bull, and they rejoice under the command of Bradhna.
They shine with far-reaching luster, brilliantly radiant; their host is the nourishing *iḷā*, and their song is majestic.

And they have brought forth a cry of praise from their two great parents, proclaiming the strength of the mighty ones, where the Bull, at the end of night, has carried the singer toward his own abode.
With five Adhvaryus, the seven sages guard the beloved, hidden station of the bird. Moving forward, the ageless bulls rejoice; for the gods have followed the ordinances of the gods.
The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first...
The many reins strive for the great steed, for the bull, the wondrous one; they are easy to guide.

O divine Hotṛ, most joyful and wise, bring hither the great gods and the two worlds, Rodasī. O Draviṇas, those who offer strengthening sacrifices, with fair words and bright splendor, have sought wealth from the Dawns.
And also, O Agni, by the greatness of the earth, forgive even the sin that has been committed; grant us for our great [well-being].
O Agni, [grant] Iḷā...
They anoint you at the sacrifice, O Lord of the Forest, with divine honey, those who seek the gods.
Whatever wealth you stand upon above, grant that here; or whatever is in the dwelling within the lap of this Mother.
Being kindled and resting in front, winning for us the imperishable prayer that brings heroic sons—driving away from us all lack of understanding—rise up for our great good fortune.
Rise up, O Lord of the Forest, upon the height of the earth;
being measured with a perfect measurement, bestow splendor upon the one who bears the sacrifice.
Well-clothed and girt about, the youth has arrived; he becomes even more excellent as he is born.
The wise poets, seeking the gods with their minds and devoted to sacred study, lead him upward.
Once born, he is born again on the auspiciousness of days, increasing in the assembly and at the sacrifice.
The wise and skillful ones purify him with their inspired thought; the sage, seeking the gods, raises his voice.
O Lord of the Forest, those which pious men have set up for you, or which the axe has carved out— may those divine sacrificial posts, standing firm, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by progeny.
Those which have been hewn upon the earth and fixed, for those who extend the ladles [of oblation]— may they grant us riches.
May they, the bestowers of the field, grant us desirable wealth among the gods.
The Ādityas, Rudras, Vasus, the excellent leaders, Heaven and Earth, the Earth, and the Mid-region— may these gods, being of one accord, protect our sacrifice and raise high the banner of the rite.
Like swans moving in rows, the sacrificial posts have come to us, clothed in brilliance.
Being raised up by the sages in the east, they go as gods to the path of the gods.
Like the horns of horned animals, the sacrificial posts with their head-pieces appear clearly upon the earth.
Or, listening to the invocation of the priests, may they protect us in the contests for booty.
O Lord of the Forest, grow with a hundred branches; may we grow with a thousand branches— you whom this sharpened axe has brought forward for great good fortune.

We mortals have chosen you as our friend, O god, for our protection— the Son of the Waters, the blessed one, of splendid luster, the swift victor, who is without rival. Desiring the woods, when you went to your mothers, the waters.
O Agni, that turning back of yours is not to be forgotten, since though you were far away, you have now come hither. You have grown beyond the harshness; thus indeed are you well-disposed.
Others go forth one after another, while others sit around waiting, upon whose friendship you have relied.
He who has gone beyond all failures and beyond those who pursue him—
him the observant ones, free from guile, have found following after him, like a lion lurking in the waters. Agni, who had thus vanished, was found by them as if he had run away of his own accord.

Mātariśvan brought him hither from afar, churned forth for the gods from the distance. O bearer of oblations to the gods, mortals have seized you; for you, O youngest one, protect all sacrifices with your wisdom, O human-like one.
That auspicious power of yours, O Agni, reveals itself even to the simple-minded,
when the cattle sit together around you who have been kindled at the close of day.
Offer oblations to him, the performer of fair rites, the fierce one with purifying luster.
Worship with obedience the swift, agile, ancient, and adorable god, the messenger.
Three hundred, three thousand, and thirty-nine gods have worshipped Agni;
they sprinkled him with clarified butter, spread the sacrificial grass for him, and then established him as the Hotṛ priest.
O Agni, the wise mortals kindle you, the god and sovereign lord of all people, at the sacrifice. At the sacrifices, O Agni, they praise you as the officiating priest and the invoker.
Shine as the guardian of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*) in your own abode. He indeed who offers worship to you, Jātavedas, with kindled fuel— he, O Agni, possesses heroic strength; he prospers.
May Agni, the banner of sacrifices, come hither with the gods; may he, being anointed by the seven hotṛ-priests, come to the one who offers the oblation.
Bring forth a lofty, ancient word for Agni, the hotṛ-priest.
For the Ordainer who bears the lights of inspired songs,
let our hymns strengthen Agni, from whom the praiseworthy one was born,
he who is beautiful to behold for the sake of great strength and wealth.
O Agni, as the most excellent sacrificer at the rite, worship the gods for the one who seeks the gods.
As the joyous Hotṛ, you shine forth and overcome our adversaries.
O Purifier, shine upon us with glorious and heroic strength.
Be most intimate to your worshippers for their well-being.
The inspired poets, praising you and remaining vigilant, kindle you—
the immortal bearer of oblations, the increaser of strength.
Agni is the Hotṛ, the domestic priest of the sacrifice, the one who observes all people; he knows the sacrifice in its continuous sequence.
He is the immortal bearer of oblations, the eager messenger, well-disposed toward us.
Agni brings all things together through our prayer.
Agni, the ancient banner of sacrifice, takes notice through our prayer;
for his purpose is effective.
The gods have made Agni— the son of strength, the widely-renowned Jātavedas, the bearer of oblations—
their messenger. Unassailable, Agni is the leader of the human tribes.
Swift is the chariot, ever new; overcoming all assailants, the unimpaired will-power of the gods is Agni, most renowned for his greatness.
The mortal who offers oblations attains through his vehicle the sacrificial foods and the dwelling of the one with purifying radiance.
May we, through our prayers, obtain all the well-placed blessings of Agni.
The inspired poets [meditate] upon Jātavedas.
O Agni, may we win all desirable things in the contests for booty; for the gods have placed them in you.

O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice, drawn by our songs, like a desirable cloud; drink of this, impelled by our prayer. O Indra and Agni, together with the singer, the conscious sacrifice approaches you.
With this [soma], drink this pressed juice! I choose Indra and Agni, who delight in the seer’s song, by means of the impulse of the sacrifice;
may they both satisfy themselves here with the soma.
I invoke the two impetuous slayers of Vṛtra, the victorious and unconquered,
Indra and Agni, the greatest winners of booty. The chanters, skilled in the ways of song, sing forth hymns to you both.
O Indra and Agni, I choose strengthening nourishments.
O Indra and Agni, you two shook down the ninety forts belonging to the Dāsas,
together with a single deed.
O Indra and Agni, from the work of the waters, our prayers go forth toward you along the paths of Ṛta.
O Indra and Agni, yours are powerful dwellings and sacrificial offerings.
Your prowess in crossing the waters has been established.
O Indra and Agni, you adorn the luminous realms of heaven for the sake of booty; this heroic deed of yours is celebrated.
Sing forth a most lofty hymn to your god Agni; may he come to us with the gods, he who is the best of sacrificers, and sit upon the sacred grass.
He who is the upholder of Truth, whose skill both heaven and earth acknowledge, and whose aids follow him.
Those possessing oblations praise him; those seeking to gain wealth invoke him for protection. He is the inspired sage who guides these people, for he is indeed the master of sacrifices.
Pay homage to that Agni for you—he is the giver who wins great riches.
May Agni grant us most peaceful protections for our enjoyment,
from which he may shower wealth upon us in heaven, on earth, and in the waters.
He is the resplendent and unprecedented one, [honored] by his excellent thoughts.
The singers kindle Agni, the invoker and lord of the people.
And do thou, O Brahman, who art most invoked by the gods, protect us during our hymns.
Shine auspiciously for us, O Agni, strengthened by the Maruts, as the greatest winner of thousands.
Now, O Agni, grant us wealth consisting of thousands, offspring, and prosperity—splendid, rich in heroic strength, most excellent, and undecaying.
The joyous Hotṛ has taken his place at the assemblies; he is the true sacrificer, the wisest sage, and the one who provides all means of success.
Agni, whose chariot is lightning, the son of strength, with hair of flame, has spread his brilliance over the earth.
I offer this word of homage to you; accept it, O observer of the Eternal Law (*ṛta*), for you who are conscious, O powerful one!
Knowing, bring hither those who know; sit down in the midst upon the sacred grass (*barhis*) for our protection, O worshipful one!
Let the two Dawns, seeking booty, hasten toward you, O Agni, along the paths of the wind.
When they anoint the ancient one with oblations, they stand in the dwelling like two riders upon a chariot-seat.
And Mitra and Varuṇa, O powerful Agni, and all the Maruts sing your praise for the sake of bliss.
O Son of Strength, as you stand with your flame, spreading out the peoples like Sūrya over men;

To-day we have indeed fulfilled your desire, having approached you with uplifted hands and with homage. With a most sacrificial mind, O Agni, as a sage, sacrifice to the gods with an unwearied thought.
For from you, O Son of Strength, proceed many aids, as well as spoils of war, from you the god.
Grant us thousandfold wealth, O Agni, through truthful speech that is free from guile. To you, O Sage of wise intellect, we mortals have offered these oblations at the sacrifice, O God.
Be mindful of every well-yoked chariot; O immortal Agni, make all that palatable.
Flaming with your broad radiance, drive away our enemies, the *rakṣas* demons, and diseases.
May I abide in the protection of the great, well-protecting Agni, under the guidance of him who is easily invoked.
Be our protector at the dawning of this very dawn, be our guardian when the sun has risen.
O Agni, well-born in body, take pleasure in my hymn of praise as in your own eternal offspring.
O bull-like Agni, beholder of men, shine forth with red radiance through the many dark nights.
O Vasu, lead us and carry us across distress; O youngest one, grant us wealth according to our desire.
Shine forth, O invincible Bull Agni, having completely conquered all strongholds for the sake of prosperity.
O Jātavedas, you are the leader of the first sacrifice and the protector of the great [sacrifice], O excellent guide.
O singer, you who are wise, shining toward the gods, grant many flawless shelters.
Like a prize-winning chariot, bring us strength, O Agni; you are the one who encompasses the two well-established worlds for us.
O Bull, cause them to swell and quicken our strengths; O Agni, you are the one who milks the two worlds for us with goodly milk.
O God, shining with the gods with brilliant luster, may the ill-will of a mortal not encompass us.
O Agni, [bestow] nourishment... This Agni is the lord of great heroic power and of great good fortune.
He is the lord of wealth consisting of good offspring and cattle; he is the lord of the slayings of Vṛtra.
O Maruts, O heroes, attend upon this man who increases [your strength], in whom there are riches that augment prosperity.
They who overcome the malicious in battles, who have subdued the enemy for all time.
As such, O Agni, bounteous one, sharpen us for wealth consisting of heroic sons— O you of many splendors, for that which is most excellent, rich in progeny, free from disease, and full of vigor.
He who has made all beings subject to himself, he who has established worship among the gods.

May he strive for us among the gods, for great heroic power, for the praise of men. O Agni, do not deliver us over to thoughtlessness, nor to lack of heroes, nor to lack of cattle, O Son of Strength; nor to reproach—drive away all hostilities.
O fortunate Agni, grant us strength consisting of abundant offspring at this great sacrifice;
O thou of many glories, bestow upon us increasing wealth that brings delight and renown.
Being kindled according to the first ordinances, he who possesses all desirable things is anointed with ointments.
Flame-haired, clothed in clarified butter, the purifier, Agni—the excellent sacrificer—[is present] for the sacrifice of the gods.
Just as you, O Agni Jātavedas, being wise, performed the office of the Hotṛ for the earth and for heaven, even so with this oblation sacrifice to the gods; like Manu, further this sacrifice today.

Three are your lifespans, O Jātavedas; three are your births from the dawns, O Agni. With these, as the one who knows, sacrifice for the protection of the gods, and then become the source of peace and well-being for the sacrificer.
Praising Agni, the beautiful-rayed and fair-to-behold, we pay homage to you, O Jātavedas, worthy of praise.
The gods have made you their messenger, their steward, and the bearer of oblations—the navel of immortality.

O Agni, that Hotṛ who was before you, more skilled in sacrifice, established in two ways, and auspicious by his own nature—to him, O wise one, sacrifice according to his law, and then establish our rite for us.
O Agni, be well-disposed toward us when we approach you; be as a friend to a friend, as kind as a father to a son.
For the settlements of men are full of many wrongdoers; burn up the hostile ones as they turn against you.
O Agni, burn the enemies within; burn away the curse of the hostile stranger.
O Vasu, you who are observant, burn those who are mindless; let your ageless, tireless flames spread out.

O Agni, desiring [success], I offer this oblation with fuel and clarified butter for the sake of speed and strength. As much as I am able, praising you with a prayer, I offer this divine hymn for the attainment of a hundredfold wealth.
O Son of Strength, being praised, bestow great vital power through your flame upon those who labor in worship.
O Agni, bestow wealth and well-being upon the Viśvāmitras; we have purified your body many times over.

Grant us treasure, O bounteous giver of riches, for you indeed become such, O Agni, when you are kindled. In the dwelling of the fortunate praiser, you hold out your broad arms and display wondrous forms, full of splendor.
I choose Agni as the Hotṛ priest at this sacrifice—the skillful sage, the all-knowing, the unerring.
May he, the most excellent sacrificer, worship among the gods for us; may he win us wealth, strength, and bounties.
O Agni, I offer to you this ladle filled with oblations, radiant, full of gifts, and dripping with clarified butter.
Moving clockwise, seeking the assembly of gods, he has established the sacrifice with gifts and treasures.
O Agni, favored by you with a most brilliant mind, grant us aid; O Giver, bestow upon us wealth consisting of noble offspring.
O Agni, may we be among the foremost in the abundance of your most heroic riches and in the praise of your excellence.
For many are the faces that have been placed in you, O Agni, as the worshipful people honor you, the god.
O youngest one, bring hither the assembly of gods, for today you shall sacrifice to the divine host.
When the gods anointed you as the Hotṛ-priest at the sacrificial meal, seating you for the performance of the rite.
As such, O Agni, be mindful of us here for our protection; bestow glorious renown upon our bodies.
At the break of dawn, the priest invokes with hymns Agni, the Aśvins, and Dadhikrā.
May the gods, possessing excellent light, hear us—united in spirit and longing for the sacrifice.

O Agni, three are your strengths, three your abodes, and three are your ancient tongues, O you who are born of Truth. Three are your bodies beloved by the gods; with these, protect our hymns without fail.
O Agni Jātavedas, many are your names, O self-dependent god of immortality.
And those many illusions of the illusionists which they have directed toward thee, O all-pervading one, whose kinship is sought after—
Agni is the leader of the divine races like Bhaga, the god who guards the seasons and upholds the cosmic order.
As the ancient slayer of Vṛtra and possessor of all wealth, may he carry the singer across all difficulties.
I invoke for this place Dadhikrā, Agni, and the goddess Uṣas, Bṛhaspati and the god Savitṛ, the Aśvins, Mitra and Varuṇa, Bhaga, the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas.
O Jātavedas, place this sacrifice of ours among the immortals; graciously accept these oblations.
O Agni, O Hotṛ, sit down as the first and partake of the drops of fat and ghee.
O Purifier, for you the drops of fat mixed with ghee drip down. According to your own nature, bestow upon us the most excellent treasure for the feast of the gods.
For you, O Agni, the wise and true one, drip the drops of ghee;
as the most excellent seer, you are kindled—be the protector of the sacrifice.
For you, O impetuous and powerful Agni, drip the drops of fat and of ghee.
Praised by the seer with a great luster, come as a god; O wise one, enjoy the oblations.
The most powerful fat has been extracted from your midst; we offer it to you.
O Vasu, the drops drip upon your skin; O God, accept them in due order.
This is that Agni in whom Indra, longing for him, placed the pressed Soma within his belly;
having won thousandfold booty like a swift steed, you are praised, O Jātavedas.
O Agni, worthy of sacrifice, that splendor of yours which is in heaven, on earth, in the plants, and in the waters—[that is yours].
By which you have spread out the wide mid-air—that radiant, surging light, the beholder of men.

O Agni, you go toward the flood of heaven; you shine toward the gods for their sake. Those waters which are in the luminous realm beyond the sun, and those which stand below it—[all these you encompass].
May the fires of the soil, in harmony with those of the flowing waters, accept the sacrifice— free from malice, free from disease, and bestowing great nourishment.
O Agni, [bestow] *iḷā*...
Rubbed forth and well-established in his dwelling, the youthful sage, the leader of the sacrifice—Agni, the ageless one among the aging woods; here Jātavedas has established immortality.
The two Bharatas, Devaśravas and Devavāta, have rubbed forth the wealthy, highly skillful Agni.
O Agni, look out with your great [light] for wealth; be our leader through the days to come.
The ten fingers have generated the ancient one, well-born and beloved among his mothers. Praise Agni, the son of Devavāta, O Devaśravas—he who shall become the master of men.

I have established you in the best place on earth, in the station of *iḷā*, on the auspiciousness of days. O Agni, shine forth with wealth upon the *dṛṣadvatī*, the *āpayā*, and the *sarasvatī* frequented by men.
O Agni, [shine upon] *iḷā*.
O Agni, overcome the hostile armies, casting away those who oppose us;
invincible, crossing over those who offer no gifts, bestow splendor upon the one who brings the sacrifice.
O Agni, you are kindled with the *iḷā* offering, the immortal invoker whom men delight to serve.
Be pleased with our sacrifice,
O Agni, wakeful one, son of strength, you who are invoked with oblations;
sit upon this sacred grass (barhis).
O Agni, together with all the Agnis and the gods, magnify my songs at the sacrifices—
those who are the seekers.
O Agni, grant wealth consisting of heroic sons and abundance to the donor; sharpen us so that we may possess many sons.
O Agni, you are the wise son of Heaven and the son of Earth, the possessor of all knowledge.
Sacrifice here to the gods individually, O wise one!
Agni, being the knower, wins heroic powers; he wins booty, striving for immortality.
O you who abound in food, bring the gods here to us!
Agni, the unerring one, illumines heaven and earth, the two immortal goddesses who belong to all people; he dwells among them, radiant with many strengths through our homages.
O Agni and Indra, come here to the sacrifice in the house of the donor who has pressed the Soma.
The gods, not failing, [came] for the drinking of Soma.
O Agni, son of strength, Jātavedas, you are kindled eternally in the dwelling of the waters;
magnifying the places of assembly with your aid.
Having perceived Agni Vaiśvānara with our minds, we, possessing oblations, sing praise to him who is worthy of invocation and the finder of heaven.

Seeking wealth, we Kuśikas call with songs upon the god who gives good gifts, the charioteer, and the delightful one. We invoke that brilliant Agni for protection—Vaiśvānara, Mātariśvan, the one worthy of hymns.
Bṛhaspati, the inspired sage, the listener, the guest who hastens swiftly for the service of the gods among men—

like a neighing horse, Vaiśvānara is kindled by the Kuśikas with their generations, age after age. May that Agni, ever-watchful among the immortals, bestow upon us heroic strength, abundance of horses, and treasure.
Let the Vājas go forth with their powers like fires; joined together for glory, they have yoked their spotted deer.
The Maruts, great oxen and possessors of all wealth, cause the mountains to tremble, they who are invincible.
The Maruts, adorned with fire and belonging to all people—we implore them for their fierce and terrible protection.
Those roaring sons of Rudra, clothed in rain, like lions in their impetuous fury, are bounteous givers.
We pray with excellent hymns for every troop, for every host—the brilliance of Agni and the might of the Maruts.
With spotted deer as steeds, possessing inexhaustible wealth, they come to the sacrifice, wise in the assemblies.
I am Agni, by birth Jātavedas; clarified butter is my eye, immortality is in my mouth. I am the threefold hymn, the measurer of the mid-region, the unaging heat; "oblation" is my name.
With three purifiers he has purified the hymn, discerning with his heart and mind the light.
By his own powers, he has made the highest treasure; from the beginning, he surveyed heaven and earth.
The inexhaustible fountain with a hundred streams, the wise father of words— Him who rejoices as a festival-singer in the lap of his parents, O Heaven and Earth, fulfill him with true speech.
May your strengths, directed toward heaven and accompanied by oblations, go forth with the ladle dripping with ghee;
may they go to the gods seeking their favor. I praise Agni with my song—the wise one, the accomplisher of the sacrifice.
