Being kindled at the sacrifice, Agni is the purifier, worthy of praise; we pray to him whose hair is flame. Broad-chested, immortal, clothed in ghee, and well-invoked with *svāhā*, he is the one we seek.
Agni is the carrier of oblations for the sacrifice. Him, the pressing priests with uplifted ladles, possessing the sacrifice, have thus brought hither with their prayer for his protection.
The immortal god, the Hotṛ, goes before by means of his creative power, impelling the assemblies of knowledge.
Like a prize-winning steed, he is placed in the contests for booty; he is led forward in the sacrificial rites.
The sage is the accomplisher of the sacrifice;
through his inspired thought, he has become most excellent. He has received the germ of beings, the father of Dakṣa, through his own body.
I have established you, the most excellent one, the one strengthened by strength, through the praise of skillful power— O Agni, the radiant and yearning one.
[They have established] Agni, the controller, the swift one, for the harnessing of the *ṛta*, as those who strive [for it].
The inspired poets kindle [him] with sacrificial offerings. I praise Agni, the Son of Strength, who shines at the sacrifice toward heaven, the one possessed of the wisdom of a seer.
Worthy of invocation and homage, visible even through the darkness— Agni,
the bull, has been kindled.
Agni, the bull, is kindled like a horse that carries the gods;
him, the possessors of oblations, magnify.
O Bull, we who are bulls ourselves shall kindle thee, the Bull.
O Agni, shine forth mightily!
O Agni, Jātavedas, graciously accept our oblation, the *puroḍāśa* cake,
at the morning pressing, O you who are enriched by prayer.
O Agni, the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāś*) has been baked for you, or rather, it has been fully prepared;
enjoy it, O youngest one!
O Agni, partake of the sacrificial cake offered on the day before yesterday.
The son of strength is established at the sacrifice;
O Jātavedas, O Sage, enjoy the sacrificial cake here at the midday libation.
O Agni, the wise do not diminish your portion at the assemblies, for you are the mighty one.
O Agni, at the third libation, take pleasure in the sacrificial cake offered to you, O Son of Strength.
Then, with skillful praise, establish among the gods the sacrifice, rich in treasures and watchful among the immortals.
O Agni Jātavedas, increasing, [accept] the oblation and the sacrificial cake.
Be pleased with that which belongs to the day after.
Here is the wood for friction; here is the means of generation prepared. Bring hither this mistress of the people; let us churn Agni as of old.
Jātavedas has been deposited in the two kindling woods, well-contained like an embryo within pregnant women;
Agni is to be praised day by day by watchful men who bring oblations.
O wise one, place him upon her who lies extended; she, having been impregnated, has immediately brought forth the bull.
The ruddy-peaked one, whose brilliance is radiant, the son of *iḷā*, has been born according to the sacred law.
We place you, O *jātavedas*, upon the footprint of *iḷā*, upon the navel of the earth, O Agni, so that you may carry our oblation.
O men, churn the sage who is free from duplicity, the wise one, the immortal with the beautiful countenance.
O men, generate Agni—the banner of sacrifice, the first in the east—who is most gracious. When they churn him with their arms, he shines forth like a spirited, ruddy stallion among the woods.
Like a brilliant horse on its course, the Aśvins' [chariot] moves unrestrained; burning up grass and stones, it passes over them.

Once born, Agni shines forth, observant, a prize-winner, a sage praised by seers, a bounteous giver— Him whom the gods have established at the sacrifices as the one to be magnified, the all-knowing bearer of oblations.

Sit down, O Hotṛ, in your own place, being wise; establish the sacrifice in the womb of good deeds. As one who pleases the gods, worship the gods with the oblation; O Agni, bestow great vitality upon the sacrificer.
O friends, produce smoke like a bull; go toward the prize of victory without faltering.
This Agni is the conqueror of armies, possessed of excellent heroes, by whom the gods overcame the Dasyus.
This is your seasonal birthplace, from which, once born, you shone forth;
knowing it, O Agni, sit down here and then cause our songs of praise to prosper.
He is called Tanūnapāt when he is the embryo of the Asura; he becomes Narāśaṃsa when he is born.
When Mātariśvan measured him out in the mother, he became the emission of Vāta in his wandering.
Well-rubbed, he is rubbed forth; well-placed, the sage is placed down.
O Agni, perform the sacrifice well; worship the gods for the one who seeks the gods.
Mortals have generated the immortal one—the tireless, swift one with strong jaws.
The ten unwedded sisters, coming together, grasp the newborn male.
The seven-hotted one shone forth from of old when he blazed up in his mother’s lap, in her udder.
Day by day the joyous one does not close his eyes, since he was born from the belly of the Asura.
Armed against the enemy, like the onset of the Maruts, the first-born of the sacred word (brahman) knows all this.
The Kuśikas have offered glorious prayer; each one in his own home has kindled Agni.
Since today, at the commencement of this sacrifice, we have chosen you here, O wise Hotṛ, you have indeed performed the rite steadfastly and with zeal; knowing and perceiving, come to the Soma.
The Soma-loving friends desire you; they press the Soma and present the sacrificial offerings.
They endure the insults of men, for there is no other source of wisdom but you, O Indra.
Even the most distant realms are not far for you; come hither, O Lord of Bay Steeds, with your two bay horses.
For the steadfast bull, these libations have been prepared; the pressing-stones are harnessed while the fire is kindled.

Indra, the fair-cheeked, the munificent, the overcomer, the one of the great host, the many-acting, the impetuous—when you, the fierce one, were placed among mortals as a protector, where then, O Bull, are those heroic deeds of yours?
For you alone, shaking even what is unshakable, go forth slaying the Vṛtras.
Heaven and earth, the mountains—even they stand as if fixed for your ordinance.
And in safety, O much-invoked one, you, the slayer of Vṛtra, have alone spoken with firmness through your glories.
Even these two boundless worlds, O Indra, when you grasp them together, O Maghavan, are but a handful to you.
Go forth, O Indra, with your two bay horses down the steep slope; let your thunderbolt go forth, crushing the enemies.
Slay those who face you, those who follow from behind, and those who flee away; make all truth prevail, and let it be spread abroad.
The mortal to whom Dhāyu granted [a portion], he shares in the domestic wealth that was not yet his.
O Indra, auspicious is your favor, dripping with clarity; O Much-invoked one, your gift bestows thousands.
O Much-invoked Indra, you crushed Kuṇāru, who dwelt together with Dānu, until he was sightless.

O Indra, with your might you struck down Vṛtra, the swelling, malevolent one who was footless. O Indra, you have established the vigorous, great, and boundless earth in its place according to its nature. The Bull has propped up the sky and the mid-air; let the waters flow here, impelled by you.
O Indra, Vala, the enclosure of the cattle, was pierced by you, the Alātr̥ṇa; fearing before your blow, he opened wide.
He made the paths easy to travel for the release of the cows; the voices of those blowing [the trumpets] gave aid to the one invoked by many.
Alone, O Indra, you filled the two world-halves, the earth and the heaven, which stand together and possess all wealth.
And from the mid-air, O Hero, bring to us in battle food and steeds yoked together, like a charioteer.

The Sun does not diminish the quarters of space as they are assigned day after day, impelled by the Lord of the Tawny Steeds. When he has traversed his paths with his horses, he then effects their unyoking; that indeed is his work.
All desire to behold the great and wondrous face of the radiant Dawn as she comes upon the path of night.
All recognize her when she has arrived in her majesty; many are the well-performed deeds of Indra.
A great light is deposited within her womb; the cow moves about bearing the ripe milk, though it is yet unripe.
RV_03.030.14.2 All sweetness has been gathered in the cow, which Indra bestowed upon her for our nourishment.
RV_03.030.15.1 Indra, be firm! The snares have been set. Aid the sacrifice for the singer and his friends.
RV_03.030.15.2 The mortals who employ deceit, who are evil-minded, who carry quivers—those enemies must be slain.
The clamor is heard from the nearby enemies; strike down the most scorching thunderbolt upon those who are low.
Cut them down from below, shatter them, and overcome them; slay the *rakṣas*, O Maghavan, and subject them to our will.
Uproot the *rakṣas* with its very root, O Indra; cut its middle and crush its tip.
How long have you acted as a destroyer? Cast your burning weapon at the hater of prayer.
O Leader, when you come with the prize-winners for our well-being, may you sit down upon many great nourishments.
May we be winners of vast wealth; let there be Indra-like, progeny-bestowing fortune within us.
O Indra, bring us glorious fortune; may we take possession of the surplus of your gift.
Our desire has spread out like the wide ocean; fulfill it, O Lord of Wealth, for you are the master of riches.
Satisfy this longing with cattle and horses, and extend it with radiant wealth.
Seeking the light with their hymns, the wise Kuśikas have fashioned a vehicle for you, O Indra.
O Lord of the Cows, burst open the enclosures for us; let prizes and strengths come to us together.
You dwell in heaven, O Bull of true vigor; O Maghavan, be a generous giver of cattle to us.

We invoke the auspicious Maghavan Indra for aid in this battle, the most heroic in the winning of booty—him who hears us, the fierce one for our protection in conflicts, the slayer of Vṛtras, the conqueror of riches.
The priest, instructing, has reached the granddaughter of his daughter; knowing the ordinance of *ṛta*, he honors its contemplation.
Where the father, seeking the union with his daughter, hastened with a willing mind; he did not leave the inheritance to his sister, but made the embryo the treasure-store of the winner.
When the mothers generated the bearer, one was the doer of good deeds, while the other was the one who cried out.
Agni was born, trembling with his tongue, as the sons of the Great One were manifested before the ruddy one.
Great is the embryo; great is he who has been born from them; great is the growth of the one whose steed is bay, through sacrifices.
Victorious powers have approached him as he contended; they recognized the great light emerging from the darkness.
Knowing him, the Dawns rose up to meet him; Indra alone became the lord of the kine. The wise ones pierced the firm stronghold; the seven seers sent them forward with their minds.
They found every path of *ṛta*; knowing it, he entered them with reverence.
When Saramā found the breach of the mountain, she made the great, ancient path wide for the common goal.
With swift feet, she led the way; knowing the path, she went first toward the lowing of the lowing ones.
The most inspired one came seeking as a friend; the mountain brought forth the embryo for the sake of the well-doer.

The young man, eager for the sacrifice, won [the prize] with you two; then Aṅgiras immediately became a singer of praise. The one who stands before all as a counterpart to every being, he knows all births and slays Śuṣṇa.
May he, the path-finder from heaven, the winner of cattle, our friend, singing our praises, release us from blame.
With minds longing for cattle, they settled down with hymns, preparing a path toward immortality.
This indeed is their abundant dwelling-place, by which they have sought to win the months through the Eternal Law (*ṛta*). Beholding it, they rejoiced, milking the milk of the ancient seed.
Their roar has heated the two worlds, heaven and earth; at their birth, they established their firm standing among the cattle and the heroes.
He, the slayer of Vṛtra, by means of his offspring, oblations, and hymns, Indra released the ruddy cows upward.
For him, the noble cow, widely ranging and bearing clarified butter, has yielded honey-sweet, delicious milk.
They have prepared a seat for him, the Father; the well-doers have looked upon his great, radiant splendor.
Supporting the two parents with a pillar, they established the impetuous one rising upward.
When the great Dhiṣaṇā (the Holy Thought) impelled him, he grew instantly, pervasive throughout heaven and earth.
In whom the blameless, harmonious songs and all invincible powers converge for Indra.
I desire your great friendship and your powers; many teams go forth to the slayer of Vṛtra.
We have come with a great hymn of praise to the Hero; O Maghavan, be our good protector.
Having found a vast domain, radiant with much light, he established from of old for his friends a path for their journeying.

Indra, shining forth, brought forth together with the men the sun, the dawn, the way, and Agni. This powerful lord of the house, even as he looked upon the waters, sent forth the all-luminous streams flowing together.
Being purified by the poets with filters, the flowing streams of honey are urged on by days and nights.
The two dark treasuries of wealth, worthy of sacrifice, yield themselves up through the greatness of the Sun.
O Indra, when your beloved, darting companions seek to encompass your majesty.
Become the lord of true blessings, O slayer of Vṛtra; you are the bull of all songs, the giver of vital strength for all life.
Come to us with your auspicious friendships, you who are great and hasten to help with your mighty succors.
Honoring him with reverence like an Aṅgiras, I fashion this new hymn for the ancient one, so that he may grant his favor.
Drive away the many godless deceivers; O Maghavan, bestow upon us what we seek for our gain.
The purifying mists have spread far and wide; carry us safely across them.
O Indra, you who are the charioteer, protect us from harm; quickly, very quickly, make us winners of cattle.

The slayer of Vṛtra, the lord of cattle, has assigned the cows; he has gone through the black ones with his ruddy domains. Bestowing pleasant truths according to the *ṛta*, he has thrown open all his own doors.
We invoke Śuna for our welfare...
O Indra, Lord of Soma, drink this Soma, this midday libation which is dear to you. Puffing out your cheeks, O Bounteous One, O Consumer of the Residue, unyoke your two bay steeds and rejoice here.
Drink the Soma mixed with milk, stirred with meal, and bright, O Indra; we have offered it to you for your exhilaration.

In harmony with the host of Maruts who perform the *brahman*, and with the Rudras, pour down [the rain] to your heart's content. O Indra, those Maruts who increased your breath, your strength, and your vigor while singing praises—
at the midday libation, O wielder of the thunderbolt, drink together with the Rudras, O fair-cheeked one, you who are accompanied by your host.

The Maruts who were there, that vigorous host of Indra, have indeed now proclaimed his sweetness— the Maruts by whom, when impelled, he found the vital spot of Vṛtra, even though he thought himself invulnerable. Like a man, O Indra, enjoying the libation, drink the Soma for eternal heroic power.
O Lord of the bay horses, turn hither with our sacrifices; together with the rushing [Maruts], you set the watery floods in motion.
When you had slain Vṛtra, O Indra, you released the waters to flow like swift steeds, as they were lying there.
With your weapon, O Indra, you struck down the godless one who had encompassed the goddesses on all sides.
Let us worship with homage Indra, the exalted, the vast, the sublime, the ageless, the youthful;
he, the worthy of sacrifice, whose greatness both beloved worlds have measured, yet even the two worlds cannot fully measure his majesty.
The deeds of Indra are many well-performed; all the gods do not violate his ordinances.
He who supported this earth and this heaven, he of wondrous deeds, begot the sun and the dawn.
O Indra, free from guile, that is your true greatness: that as soon as you were born, you drank the Soma.
Neither the days, O Indra, nor the days and nights, nor the months, nor the autumns can restrain the power of you, the mighty one.
As soon as you were born, O Indra, you drank the Soma for exhilaration in the highest heaven;
when you pervaded heaven and earth, you then became the ancient sustainer of the poets.
O many-born one, being more powerful, you slew the dragon who lay encompassing the waters, displaying his might.
The heaven did not equal your greatness when you stood upon the earth with one hip alone.
For the sacrifice, O Indra, has been your strengthener; it is dear to you, as is the pressed soma and the sacrificial food.
Being worthy of worship, protect sacrifice after sacrifice; the sacrifice aided your thunderbolt for the slaying of the great dragon.

With sacrifice and protection, I have brought Indra hither; may I turn him toward us for new favor. He who has grown strong through ancient hymns, through those of the middle ages, and even through the newest—since the creative impulse has entered me and brought me forth, I shall praise Indra before the decisive day.
Where he may carry us across distress, as one calls out to both sides of a ship as it moves along— Full is his beaker; *svāhā*! Like a pourer, I have poured the vessel for him to drink.
The dear Soma drops have turned together toward Indra for exhilaration, moving in a clockwise direction.
Neither the deep-flowing river, O much-invoked one, nor the mountains surrounding you have held you back. Thus urged by your friends, O Indra, you shattered even the firm enclosure of the cattle-pen.
Let us invoke Śuna for our welfare...
From the lap of the mountains, longing [for you], like two mares let loose, vying with each other;
like two bright mother-cows licking [their calves], the Vipāś and Śutudrī rush forth with their waters. Impelled by Indra, seeking his impulsion, you two go toward the ocean like two chariot-drivers.
Moving together, swelling with their waves, one after another they pass into each other, O radiant ones.
I have approached the Sindhu, the most motherly; we have gone to the broad and auspicious Vipāś.
Licking each other like two mother-cows their calf, they move together along their common source.
Swelling with this milk, we move along the god-fashioned womb;
our impetus, once set in motion, cannot be turned back. What does the inspired singer desire as he calls aloud to the rivers?
O you who are true to the *ṛta*, take delight for a moment in my Soma-like word with your swift movements.
With a lofty hymn of praise, seeking aid, the son of Kuśika has called toward the river.
Indra, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, dug out our channels; he struck down Vṛtra, the barrier of the rivers.
The god Savitṛ, the fair-handed, led us forth; by his impulse we travel across the wide expanses.
This heroic deed of Indra must be proclaimed forever—that he tore apart the dragon. With his thunderbolt, he struck down those who sat around him; the waters went forth, seeking their course.
O singer, do not forget these words, for they shall reach you in future generations as your shouts of praise.
O singer, take pleasure in our hymns; do not strike us down among men—homage be to you! O sisters, listen well to the singer; he has come to you from afar with food upon his chariot.
Bow down low; become easy to cross for us—O rivers, flow downward with your currents below the axle!
O *kārū*, let us hear your words; you have come from afar with your wagon and chariot.
I bow down before you like a swelling woman, like a maiden for her suitor; I shall ever praise you.
When indeed the Bharatas, seeking cattle, shall cross over you—driven by desire, impelled by Indra—in that village...

Let the impulse flow forth, urged by the impulse; I choose the favor of you who are worthy of sacrifice. The Bharatas, seeking cattle, have crossed over; the sage has obtained the favor of the rivers.
Swell forth, you who provide nourishment and great wealth; fill your bellies and flow swiftly!
Let your wave, O waters, strike with the yoke-pin; release the thongs.
Let the two inviolable cows, though they have committed sin and are stained by guilt, not perish.
Indra, the finder of wealth, bestowing gifts, shattered the Dāsa with his hymns and struck down the enemies.
Impelled by the sacred word (*brahman*), increasing in body, and bestowing abundant gifts, you have filled both worlds, heaven and earth.
I send forth my voice to celebrate the impetus of you, the mighty and sacrificial one, adorning it for the sake of the immortal.
O Indra, you are the first to go before the human settlements and the divine tribes alike.
Indra, whose way is to destroy, encompassed Vṛtra; he, whose way is to transform, overcame the wiles of the guileful.
He struck down Vyansa, burning among the woods, and made manifest the voices of the nights.
Indra, the winner of light, generating the days, conquered the hostile armies with his helpers, being the one who comes to our aid.
They made the banner of days shine for Manu; he found the light of the Great One for his struggle.
Indra entered with his impetuous might, bestowing many heroic deeds like a man. He has inspired these prayers for the singer; he has extended their bright hue.
They celebrate the many great deeds well-performed by this great Indra.
With his encircling strength he crushed the crooked ones; with his wondrous powers, he of surpassing might, overcame the Dasyus.
Through battle, Indra by his greatness created wide space for the gods—the true lord, the filler of the people.

In the dwelling of Vivasvat, the inspired poets and sages praise these deeds of his with hymns. They celebrate him who is all-conquering, most excellent, the giver of strength, who has won the light and the divine waters; they rejoice after Indra, the wise one, who has won both this earth and the heavens.
Indra won the coursers and he won the sun; Indra won the cow that provides much nourishment.
He won golden wealth and enjoyment; having slain the Dasyus, he protected the Aryan race.
Indra won the plants and the waters; he won the trees and the mid-air.
He split Vala and drove away the disputants; then he became the tamer of those with hostile intentions.
May we invoke Śuna for good fortune...
Mount the two bay steeds upon the chariot; being yoked, come toward us like Vāyu with his teams of horses.
Drink the soma-juice poured forth for us; O Indra, Svāhā! We have offered it for your exhilaration.
I yoke the two swift bay steeds, the much-invoked ones, to the poles of the chariot, so that they may run swiftly and bring Indra hither to this sacrifice from every side, even from afar.
Bring hither the two vigorous ones, O Tapuṣpāt; do thou likewise, O self-dependent Bull.
Let the two horses devour [the fodder]; unyoke here the two ruddy steeds. Day by day, let them be fed with similar portions of nourishment.
With a sacred prayer, I yoke for thee the two swift bay horses, thy companions, who share the feast and are yoked by prayer.
Mounting your firm and comfortable chariot, O Indra, come to the Soma as one who is wise and discerning.
Let not other sacrificers detain your two vigorous, broad-backed bay steeds.
Pass by them all; we shall prepare for you what is sufficient with the pressed Somas.
This Soma is yours; come hither, O Indra, and being well-disposed, drink it most constantly. Having sat down upon the sacrificial grass at this sacrifice, O Indra, take this drop into your belly.
The sacrificial grass is strewn for you, O Indra, the Soma is pressed, and the parched grains are prepared for your two bay steeds to eat.

To you, whose dwelling is that [place], the many-powered bull accompanied by the Maruts—to you the oblations have been offered. O Indra, the men, the mountains, and the waters have made this [soma] sweet with milk for you.
Having come, O lofty one, drink it with a gracious mind, knowing well and perceiving your own paths.
O Maruts, those whom you did not share in the Soma, O Indra— those who strengthened you and became your host—

with them, being of one mind and desiring it, drink this Soma with the tongue of Agni, O Indra. O Indra, drink of the pressed juice according to your own nature, or drink with the tongue of Agni, O worshipful one!
O Śakra, enjoy the offering prepared by the *adhvaryu* from his hand, or the sacrifice and oblation of the *hotṛ*.
May we invoke auspiciousness...
May you establish this very presentation for our gain, approaching with constant messengers at every single moment.
At every pressing he has grown strong with his increasing powers, he who has become renowned through his great deeds.
For Indra, the Soma juices have been known since ancient times—those by which he became the far-reaching R̥bhu with bull-like joints.
Welcome these as they are being offered; O Indra, drink of the vigorous bull shaken by the strong ones.

Drink and grow strong; for yours indeed are the pressed Soma-draughts, O Indra—both those of old and these here now. Just as you drank the ancient Somas, O Indra, so drink them today, O Wondrous One, as one who is newer.
Great is he in this assembly, overflowing in the conflict; fierce is his power, and he possesses bold vigor.
Neither the earth nor I could contain him when the Soma juices exhilarated the Lord of the Bay Steeds.
Great and fierce, he has grown for heroic power; the Bull has gathered himself through poetic wisdom.
Indra is the giver of fortune; his cows bestow booty; his sacrificial gifts (dakṣiṇās) are born forth in abundance.
When the rivers have gone forth according to their impulse, as waters flow toward the ocean like charioteers;
even wider than that seat is Indra, when the Soma, the pressed stalk, satisfies him.
The rivers, flowing together with the ocean, bring the well-pressed Soma for Indra.
The skilful-handed ones milk the stalk with their arms; they purify the honey with streams through the filters.
Like lakes are his bellies that hold the Soma; he has encompassed many libations at once. When Indra had consumed the first foods and slain Vṛtra, he chose the Soma for himself.
Bring it hither; let nothing stand in the way of this! For we know you to be the lord of riches.
O Indra, O master of bay horses, bestow upon us that magnificent gift which is yours.
O bounteous Indra, O impetuous one, grant us abundant wealth that contains all desirable things.
Grant us a hundred autumns to live, O Indra, and grant us perpetual heroic sons, O fair-cheeked one!
We invoke Śuna for aid...
For the sake of power that slays Vṛtra and for victory in battle.
O Indra, we turn you hither;
O Śatakratu, may the worshippers bring your mind and your eye toward us, O Indra.
O Śatakratu, we invoke all your names with every song for the sake of overcoming our adversaries, O Indra. With the hundred powers of you who are praised by many, we magnify you.
Of Indra, the sustainer of the people. I invoke Indra, who is invoked by many, for the slaying of Vṛtra,
in battles for the winning of booty.
Be victorious in the contests for booty; we implore you, O Śatakratu, O Indra, to slay Vṛtra.
[Be victorious] in glorious battles, in the struggle for the prize, in the overcoming of enemies, and in the quest for renown.
O Indra, be victorious over those who attack us! O Indra, for our protection, drink the most powerful, glorious, and watchful Soma,
O Śatakratu.
O Śatakratu, those senses of yours which are among the five peoples—O Indra, I choose those very ones from you.
O Indra, you have attained great renown; bestow upon us invincible splendor.
We increase your strength.
Come to us from nearby, O Śakra, or even from afar;
for that world of yours exists here, O wielder of the thunderbolt—come hither from there, O Indra!
Like a carpenter, I have fashioned this thought with my inspired mind, like a prize-winning steed with a well-yoked harness, speeding forward.
Touching upon the most beloved secrets of the ancient sages, I, the wise one, desire to behold them.
Furthermore, ask about the lineage of the sages; they who uphold the mind and perform good deeds have carved out the heavens.
These swelling streams of thine, impelled by thought, now come according to the sacred law.

Here they have settled down, concealing their secret powers, anointing both worlds for the sake of sovereign rule. They have measured them out with their proportions, stretched wide, and joined together; the two great ones have been established within for the sake of sustenance.
All have honored him as he was mounting; clothed in splendors, he moves with self-resplendence.
That is the great name of the Bull, the Asura; assuming all forms, he has taken his stand upon the immortal realms.
The first Bull, the elder, brought them forth; these many powers of his exist in abundance.
O Sons of Heaven, O Kings, through the insights of the assembly, you have maintained sovereign power from days of old.

O two Kings, you encompass the three, the many, and all the seats of the assembly. There, having traveled in spirit, I beheld with my mind the Gandharvas within the sacred law, those whose hair is the wind.
Then indeed, by means of names, they measured out the kinship of this bull, the milch-cow;
the wise ones, clothing themselves in various divine powers, fashioned their form within him.
Then indeed, like a bird, Savitar extended his golden wisdom upon its path.
With our excellent praise, may we attract the all-encompassing Heaven and Earth; like a maiden concealing her offspring, they have covered themselves.

You two accomplish the ancient and great work; may you both be our divine protection on every side. All the wise ones behold the manifold deeds of the one who stands firm, whose tongue is the guardian of cattle.
RV_03.038.10.1 We invoke for our welfare...
RV_03.039.01.1 The hymn, fashioned from praise, goes forth from the heart toward Indra, the Lord, as it is being uttered.
RV_03.039.01.2 O Indra, you who are ever-watchful at the sacrifice when the hymn is recited, take note of that which is born for you.

Born from heaven itself as the first of all, wide-awake and being recited at the sacrifice—clad in auspicious, bright garments, this is that ancient ancestral prayer of ours. Even the twin sisters, the daughters of Yama, have brought forth here; the tip of the tongue has indeed sped forth and taken its place.
The two born together, destroyers of darkness, move in unison at the base of the heat; they possess wondrous forms.
Among mortals, there is no one to revile those who are our fathers, warriors for the sake of cattle.
Indra, the majestic and powerful one, has made firm their strength; the wonder-worker has burst open the enclosures of the cows.
Where the friend, together with his friends, the Navagvas, went forth with the warriors after the cattle along the paths—
there truly Indra, with the ten Dasas, found the sun dwelling in the darkness.
Indra found the honey stored within the cow, footed and hoofed, belonging to the lowing beast.

That which was placed in the cave, the secret, hidden within the waters—the possessor of skill has taken it into his right hand. Discerning the light from the darkness, he chose it; may we be far from misfortune in the encounter.
O Indra, drinker of Soma, strengthened by Soma, take pleasure in these songs of the most frequent singer.
May light attend the sacrifice for heaven and earth; may we be far from great distress.
For even the many assaults of the impetuous mortal, O Vasus, you cross over with ease through your power.
We invoke Śuna for our welfare...
O Indra, we invoke you, the bull, when the Soma is pressed;
as such, drink of the sweet juice.
O Indra, praised by many, take pleasure in the pressed Soma that awakens the intellect.
Drink and pour yourself forth until you are satisfied!
O Indra, praised by us, O Lord of the People, further our sacrifice accompanied by all the gods, for we are intent upon it.
O Indra, these pressed Soma juices go forth for you, O Lord of the Good; the bright drops seek your dwelling. Take into your belly the pressed Soma, O Indra, the most excellent.
Thine are the celestial drops, O lover of songs; drink our pressed juice, for thou art anointed by the streams of honey.
Indra, glory is indeed won through thee alone.
The imperishable splendors of the trees attend upon Indra;
having drunk of the Soma, he has grown strong.
Come to us from nearby, and from afar as well, O slayer of Vṛtra!
Be pleased with these our songs;
since you are invoked from between the far distance and the near,
O Indra, come here from there.
Come then to us, O Indra, being invoked toward me for the drinking of the Soma; come with your two bay horses, O wielder of the stone.
The Hotṛ priest has sat down in due season; the sacrificial grass has been spread out continuously.
The stones have been yoked at dawn.
These prayers are being made for you, O you who are borne by prayers; sit upon the sacred grass. O Hero, partake of the sacrificial cake.
Rejoice in these libations of ours, O slayer of Vṛtra, in these hymns and in our songs of praise,
O Indra, lover of song!
The prayers lick the vast lord of power, the drinker of Soma.
As mothers [call] their calf, so [we call] Indra.
Rejoice indeed in the soma-juice for the sake of great bounty for yourself;
do not deliver your praiser to reproach.
O Indra, we, seeking you and bearing oblations, sing your praises;
and you, O Vasu, are well-disposed toward us.
Do not release us to the enemy; come hither, O lover of the bay steeds.
O Indra, drinker of the *svadhā*, rejoice here! O Indra, let the two long-maned horses, dripping with ghee, carry you hither on the easy-gliding chariot to sit upon the sacrificial grass.
Come to our pressed Soma, O Indra, which is mixed with milk; come with your two bay steeds that are well-disposed toward us.
Come, O Indra, to this exhilarating drink, pressed by the stones upon the sacred grass.
Would you not indeed satisfy yourself with this?
Thus do my songs, sent forth from here by the skillful singer, turn toward Indra for the drinking of the Soma.
We invoke Indra here with hymns for the drinking of the soma; will he not surely come by means of our songs of praise?
O Indra, these somas have been pressed; take them up, O Lord of a hundred powers!
O lord of plenty, [place it] within your belly;
for we know you, O Sage, as the winner of wealth, bold in battles. Therefore, we pray for your favor.
O Indra, come with your bulls and drink this pressed juice of ours, mixed with milk and mixed with barley.
O Indra, in your own dwelling, I urge you to drink the Soma.
May this [song] delight in your heart.
O Indra, we Kuśikas, seeking your aid, call upon you, the ancient one, for the drinking of the pressed soma.
Come hither, standing upon the chariot-seat; to you belongs the drinking of Soma from days of old.
Unyoke your two dear friends; these carriers of oblations call you to the sacrificial grass.
Come to us with your two bay steeds, passing over many peoples and toward our human prayers.
For these hymns, fashioned with praise, call upon you, O Indra, as they take delight in your friendship.
O God Indra, being well-pleased, come quickly with your bay steeds to our sacrifice which increases through homage.
For I invoke you repeatedly with my prayers, offering oblations of clarified butter at the feast of the sweet draughts.
And may these two vigorous bay steeds, your companions, well-yoked and fair-limbed, bring you hither;
may Indra, enjoying the libation with parched grain, as a friend hear the praises of his friend.
Will you not make me the protector of the people? Will you not make me the king, O Maghavan, O consumer of the Soma dregs?
Would that you make me a seer who has drunk of the pressed juice; would that you grant me of immortal wealth!
O Indra, let the tall, bay steeds, harnessed together, bring you hither to the feast.
They who from of old reach toward the heights of heaven, well-groomed and vigorous, are the draft-animals of the Bull.

O Indra, drink of the bull-strong [Soma] shaken by the bull-strong [pressers], which the falcon brought for you who desired it. In whose exhilaration you cause the peoples to tremble, and in whose exhilaration you threw open the cow-pens.
Let us invoke Śuna for good fortune...

May this beloved Soma, pressed by the tawny steeds, be yours. O Indra, taking pleasure in it, come to us with your tawny steeds; mount your tawny chariot. Desiring her, you caused the Dawn to shine; desiring him, you caused the Sun to glow.
O Indra, Lord of the bay horses, wise and discerning, you increase and surpass all glories.
Indra has sustained the heaven that nourishes the bay steeds and the earth that is the form of the bay;
between these two, he who possesses the bay steeds moves about, providing abundant food.
Born as a tawny bull, he illumines the entire radiant realm.
He of the bay horses takes up his tawny weapon; he holds the golden thunderbolt in his arms.
Indra grasps the desirable, bright, and pure thunderbolt, which is enveloped in light.
With his bay horses and stones, he opened [the cave] where the pressed juice was; with his bay horses, he drove forth the cows.
O Indra, come hither with your exhilarating bay horses whose manes are like peacock feathers.
Let no one hold you back, as fowlers catch a bird; pass over them like a desert.
The devourer of Vṛtra, the breaker of Vala, the destroyer of fortresses, the leader of the waters;
Indra, the driver of the chariot and the master of the two bay horses, shatters even the firmest things. Like deep-sea oceans, you nourish your power, as one tends to cattle.

Like milch-cows to their well-guarded stall, like streams flowing into a lake, let them come to us. Bring us strengthening wealth; as one who acknowledges his share, shake it down for us like ripe fruit from a tree—O Indra, bring us the treasure that carries us across.
O Indra, you are long-lived, self-ruling, of consistent purpose, and most glorious in your own fame.

Increasing in might, O much-praised one, be for us the most renowned of those who possess good renown. Of you, the warrior, the bull, the self-ruler, the fierce, the youthful, the ancient, and the impetuous—

The heroic deeds of the undecaying wielder of the thunderbolt, Indra, the famous and great, are truly great. You are great, O mighty one, by your manly powers; you are fierce, a seeker of wealth, overcoming others.
You alone are the king of the entire world; as such, lead the people into battle and cause them to dwell in peace.
He has surpassed all measures, shining forth; he has surpassed all the gods from every side, being irresistible.
By his might, Indra surpasses heaven and earth; the impetuous one surpasses the great intermediate space.
Wide, deep, formidable by birth, all-encompassing, he is the protector of prayers.
The Soma juices, pressed from of old, enter Indra as rivers flow into the ocean.

O Indra, that Soma which Earth and Heaven bear for you with love, like a mother bearing her child—that very one they urge forth for you; that very one the Adhvaryus purify for you, O Bull, so that you may drink.
O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, a bull for the battle, drink the Soma according to your wont for exhilaration.
Pour into your belly a wave of the sweet juice; you have been the king of the pressed libations from of old.
O Indra, acting in harmony with the troop of Maruts, drink the Soma, O wise hero, slayer of Vṛtra.
Slay our enemies, drive away the mockers, and then grant us safety from every side.
And, O Indra, drinker of the Soma by the seasons, drink our pressed Soma with the gods who are your friends—
those Maruts whom you shared with, who followed you and struck down Vṛtra, bestowing strength upon you.
O Maghavan, those who strengthened you at the slaying of Ahi, those at the battle with Śambara, O Lord of Bay Steeds, and those in the quest for cattle;
those sages who now rejoice after you—drink the Soma, O Indra, together with your host of Maruts.
[We invoke] Indra, the bull accompanied by the Maruts, the ever-increasing, the one whose will is never thwarted, the divine ruler.
We invoke here for our new protection that fierce one, the giver of victory, who is capable of overcoming all.

As soon as he was born, the youthful bull began to consume the pressed soma-juice. Drink of the pure juice according to your desire, for this is the first offering of the Soma mixed with milk for you.
On the day you were born, out of desire for you, O Aṃśu, you drank the nectar situated on the mountain.
Your mother, the youthful progenitor, poured that [milk] for you first into the house of the great father.
Having approached his mother, he begged for food; he gazed upon the sharp Soma from her udder.
Driving away the others, the skillful one moved; he of many forms and faces performed great deeds.
Fierce, overcoming the swift, with surpassing power, he fashioned his body according to his will.
Indra, having overcome Tvaṣṭṛ by his very birth, drank the Soma of that [demon] in those battles.
RV_03.048.05.1 We invoke for prosperity...
RV_03.049.01.1 Praise the great Indra, in whom all the people who drink Soma have fulfilled their desire;
RV_03.049.01.2 Him, the one of good wisdom, fashioned by the two worlds (Dhiṣaṇās) and by Vibhvan, whom the gods generated as the slayer of Vṛtras.
Him whom no one indeed overcomes in battles—the self-ruling, most heroic one who stands upon his bay horses;
him, the most powerful, who with his vigorous warriors has shortened the life of the Dasyu by his broad strides.
Victorious in combats, a swift steed, he has pervaded both heaven and earth, the bounteous giver.
Like Bhaga, he is to be invoked in the act of worship by our hymns; like a father, he is beautiful, easy to call upon, and the bestower of vital strength.
He is the upholder of heaven, the back of the mid-air, standing on high like Vāyu’s chariot with its teams of horses and the Vasus.
He is the illuminator of the nights, the progenitor of the sun, and the apportioner of the share of booty, like the Goddess Dhīṣaṇā.
RV 3.49.5.1: May we invoke for our prosperity...
RV 3.50.1.1: Let Indra drink [the Soma] with the cry of *svāhā*, he whose Soma [we offer], having come as a mighty bull accompanied by the Maruts.
RV 3.50.1.2: May he, the wide-extending one, be filled with these foods; may this oblation fulfill the desire of his body.
I harness for you the two attendants for speed, whose obedience you have favored since ancient times.
May the bay horses place you here, O fair-cheeked one; drink of this well-pressed, delightful soma.
Praising him for the sake of preeminence and sustenance, they have established Indra—the one who provides a good crossing—as the one who mingles with the milk.
Rejoicing, having drunk the Soma, O possessor of the *ṛjīṣa*, drive forth for us cattle in many ways.
[Fulfill] this desire...
We invoke Śuna for prosperity...
Great hymns have resounded toward Indra, the sustainer of the people, the bountiful one worthy of praise;
Toward him who has grown strong through well-fashioned songs, the much-invoked immortal who is celebrated day by day.
My hymns approach from every side Indra, the lord of a hundred powers, the ocean-like, the mighty hero.

The winner of booty, the breaker of forts, the swift one who crosses the waters, who dwells in the home, the one who comes to our aid, the finder of light— In the mine of wealth, the singer is praised; Indra, free from fault, honors those who laud him with hymns.
For he has taken delight in the dwelling-place of Vivasvat; praise him, the all-conquering slayer of the assailants.

Sing forth with songs and hymns to the Hero, the most manly among men, pressing toward him with zeal! He who possesses many wondrous powers bows down before you for the sake of conquest; from of old, homage is his alone, for he is the sole Lord. Abundant are his gifts among mortals; the earth bears many riches for him.
For Indra, the heavens, the plants, the waters, the living streams, and the forests preserve his wealth.
To you, O Indra, Lord of the Bay Steeds, the sacred prayers and songs have been offered together; accept them with pleasure.
Be mindful of our newest well-being, O Friend; as a gracious benefactor, bestow vital strength upon those who sing your praise.
O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma here, just as you drank of the pressed juice at Śāryāta’s sacrifice.
Under your guidance and in your protection, O Hero, the wise ones who perform excellent sacrifices seek to win your favor.
Therefore, O Indra, longing for it, drink our pressed Soma here together with your friends, the Maruts.
When you were born, O much-invoked one, all the gods surrounded you for the great battle;
at the crossing of the waters, the Maruts, bestowing their gifts, rejoiced after Indra.
Together with them, let the slayer of Vṛtra drink the pressed Soma in the sacrificer’s own dwelling-place.
For this [Soma] has been pressed with power; O Lord of bounties, drink of it, O lover of songs!
May he abide according to his own nature when the Soma is pressed; restrain your body [within it].
May that Soma-draught exhilarate you; may it reach your two flanks, O Indra, and through this prayer, let it reach your head, and your two arms, O Hero, for the sake of bestowing bounty.
O Indra, at dawn, enjoy our offering accompanied by parched grains, by groats, by cakes, and by hymns of praise.
O Indra, enjoy the well-baked sacrificial cake and give us your approval.
For you the oblations flow; eat our sacrificial cake and take pleasure in our songs,
as a suitor seeks after a maiden.
O you who are renowned from of old, enjoy our sacrificial cake at our morning libation;
for great, O Indra, is your creative power. O Indra, accept these parched grains of the midday libation and this pleasing sacrificial cake.
When the praiser, the singer, seeking swift gain and acting like a bull, implores you with his songs;
at the third libation, O much-praised one, grant us the parched grain and the offered sacrificial cake.
O Sage, may we, providing nourishment, serve you who are accompanied by the *Ṛbhus* and possessed of strength, through our inspired hymns.

For you who are accompanied by Pūṣan, we have prepared the groats; for you who possess bay horses and are lord of bay steeds, the parched grains. Eat the cake with your troop of Maruts; drink the Soma, O wise hero, slayer of Vṛtra.
Quickly bring forth the parched grains and the sacrificial cake for him, the most heroic among men.
Day by day, O Indra, may these similar [offerings] increase for you; may they strengthen you for the drinking of Soma, O Bold One.
O Indra and Parvata, on your lofty chariot bring hither delightful refreshments accompanied by noble heroes.
O Gods, enjoy the oblations at the sacrifices; be strengthened by our songs, rejoicing in the *iḷā*.
Stay here, O Maghavan; do not go away. Now I shall worship you with well-pressed Soma.

Like a son grasping his father’s garment, O Indra, I grasp yours with a most sweet song, O Lord of Might. O Adhvaryu, let us recite; respond to me. Let us both prepare an acceptable offering for Indra.
Sit upon this sacrificial grass of the sacrificer; let the hymn be recited for Indra.
O Maghavan, come home; that indeed is your dwelling-place. Then let your harnessed bay horses carry you hither. Whenever we shall press the Soma, Agni shall speed as your messenger toward it.
Depart, O Maghavan, and come back again; O Indra, brother, there is business for you in both places—where the great chariot is stationed and where the prize-winning donkey is unyoked.
You have drunk the Soma; O Indra, go forth to our home, bringing auspicious things and joy to your dwelling.
Where there is the stationing of the great chariot, or the unyoking of the prize-winning steeds accompanied by sacrificial gifts—
there these liberal patrons, the Aṅgirases of diverse forms, the sons of Heaven, the heroes of the Asura,
bestowing riches upon Viśvāmitra at the thousandfold libation, prolong their lives.
Maghavan assumes form after form, creating magical illusions around his own body.
When he comes from heaven three times in an instant, the observer of the cosmic order (*ṛtāvā*), who does not drink at fixed seasons, arrives with his own mantras.
The great seer, born of the gods and impelled by the gods, the watcher of men, has propped up the oceanic flood.
When Viśvāmitra brought Sudās [to the sacrifice], Indra took pleasure in him along with the Kuśikas.

Like swans, you make a sound with the pressing-stones; rejoicing with songs at the pressed soma during the rite, O inspired seers who behold men, drink together with the gods—the sweet soma-mead, O Kuśikas.
Come hither, O Kuśikas, and take heed! Release the horse for the sake of wealth for Sudās.
May the King slay Vṛtra toward the east, the west, and the north; then let him sacrifice at the best place upon the earth.
I, who have praised Indra, have lauded both these worlds, heaven and earth.

Viśvāmitra protects this Brahman-power for the Bharata people. The Viśvāmitras have offered this prayer to Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt; O bounteous one, grant us gifts as if from the hand of a liberal giver.
What do your cows do among the Kīkaṭas? They do not yield the milk-mixture, nor do they heat the *gharma* vessel.
Bring us the wealth of Pramaganda; O Maghavan, subject Naicāśākha to us.
Sasarparī, the gift of Jamadagni, has lowed loudly, driving away indolence.
The Daughter of the Sun has spread her fame among the gods— immortal and undecaying.
Sasarparī has swiftly brought this glory to these people of the five tribes,
she who, bestowing new life upon her wings, was given to me by the Palastis and the Jamadagnis.
May the two oxen be firm; may the axle be strong. Let not the two chariot-poles be shattered, nor let the yoke be broken.
May Indra protect the two side-pieces of the body; O you whose rim is uninjured, be with us.
Bestow strength upon our bodies, O Indra, and bestow strength upon our horses.

Grant strength for our children and descendants so that they may live, for you are indeed the giver of strength. Envelop yourself in the essence of the *khadira* wood; bestow vigor upon the chariot and the *śiṃśapā* wood.
O axle, be firm; being firm, hold us steady; do not let us slip away from this journey.
May this lord of the forest not abandon us, nor may he harm us— until our arrival home in safety and until our release.
O Indra, Maghavan, Hero, quicken us today with your many and most excellent aids.
May he who hates us fall low; may our life-breath abandon him whom we hate.
It heats even the axe and shatters even the *śimbala* tree. O Indra, even the cauldron, when heated and boiling over, casts out foam.
O people, they do not understand the arrow; thinking it to be a mere beast, they lead away the red one.
They do not cause the swift horse to run with the swift horses; they do not lead the donkey in front of the horses.
O Indra, these sons of Bharata have understood neither the retreat nor the advance.
They urge on the immortal steed as if it were constant; they lead him around the racecourse like a bowstring in battle.
For the great assembly, they have repeatedly offered this strength to the one worthy of praise. May Agni hear us with his domestic fires; may the eternal Agni hear us with his celestial flames.
I sing a great hymn to the great Heaven and to the Earth; my desire goes forth, seeking and knowing.
For at their praise in the assemblies, the gods who honor them rejoice together with these two.
O Heaven and Earth, let your *ṛta* be truth; be present for our great and auspicious welfare.
This homage to Heaven, O Agni, and to Earth; with an offering I worship and seek for treasure.
For indeed, the ancient ones, whose speech is true, have found you both, O Holy Ones, O Heaven and Earth.
Even men, seeking to find you, have paid homage to you both in the assembly where heroes win the prize, O Pṛthivī.
Who truly knows? Who here can declare it? Whither do these paths converge toward the gods?
Their lowest dwellings have been seen, which are in the highest secret ordinances.
The seer, who beholds men, has looked upon us; they rejoice in the two distinct wombs of *ṛta*.
They have prepared their dwelling for you as if in different places, yet they are in agreement through a common purpose.
Though separated by a common bond yet far apart, they stand at a fixed station, ever-watchful. And being young sisters, they call themselves by names that form a pair.

All these generations have been distinguished together; bearing the great gods, she does not waver. The one moving thing rules over all that is fixed, the winged bird that moves hither and thither, born diverse.
From of old, from ancient times, I have learned from afar this kinship of ours with the great Father, the progenitor.

RV_03.054.09.2 {25} Where the gods, being praised with their hymns, stood upon the wide, divergent path. RV_03.054.10.1 {25} This hymn I proclaim, O Heaven and Earth; may they of the soft entrails, whose tongue is Agni, hear it.
RV_03.054.10.2 {25} Mitra, Varuṇa the youthful sovereign, and the Ādityas, the far-extending sages.
Savitar, golden-handed, fair-tongued, ruling over the threefold assembly of heaven, has sent forth a cry of praise among the gods; O Savitar, bestow upon us complete well-being.
May the god Tvaṣṭṛ—skilled in action, fair-handed, lordly, and true to the cosmic order—grant us those things for our protection.
O *Ṛbhus*, accompanied by Pūṣan, rejoice! With the pressing-stones raised, you have fashioned the sacrifice.
The Maruts, whose chariots are lightning, who bear spears, the youths of heaven, born of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*), the tireless ones;
may Sarasvatī and the worshipful gods hear us—the swift ones, bestowing wealth along with heroic sons.
Hymns and songs of praise go forth to Viṣṇu, the one seen in many places, as singers go on the path of Bhaga.
He is the wide-striding, preeminent one, whose many youthful mothers do not neglect him.
Indra, ruling through all his heroic powers, has filled both heaven and earth with his greatness.
Purandara, slayer of Vṛtra, with your bold host, gather and bring to us abundant cattle.

The Nāsatyas are my fathers, inquiring after kinship; the Aśvins’ kinship is a lovely name. For you two are the givers of wealth among our riches; O undeceived ones, you protect the gift with those who do not withhold.
O sages, that great and beautiful name of yours is truly yours, O gods, since you exist entirely within Indra.

O much-invoked one, as a friend with your beloved Ṛbhus, fashion this prayer for us so that we may win the prize. May Aryaman, Aditi, and the worshipful ones—those who do not violate the inviolable ordinances of Varuṇa—be with us.
Keep us far from reaching childlessness; may our path be rich in progeny and cattle.
May the messenger of the gods, sent forth in many ways, declare us sinless in our integrity.
May the Earth, the Sky, and the Waters hear us, as well as the Sun with the constellations and the wide mid-air.
May the mighty mountains hear us, who are firm in their foundations and rejoice in the sacrificial food.
May Aditi, together with the Ādityas, hear us; may the Maruts grant us auspicious protection. May the path always be easy to travel and rich in nourishment; O gods, endow the plants with sweetness.
O Agni, may I not suffer harm in your friendship; may I attain a dwelling place of wealth abounding in food.
Make the oblations sweet; shine forth with nourishment toward us; measure out for us glorious renown.
O Agni, conquer all those enemies in battles; shine upon us with a gracious mind every day.

When the earliest dawns broke forth, the great imperishable syllable was born in the station of the Cow. Attending to the ordinances of the gods, the great and unique divine sovereignty of the gods has manifested.
O Agni, let not the gods here lead us astray, nor the ancient fathers who know the path.
The banner between the two ancient dwellings...
My desires fly forth in many directions; I have looked toward the ancient rites with reverence.
When the fire is kindled, let us speak only the Truth (ṛta)...
The common king, distributed in many places, lies among the resting ones, moving through the woods.
One mother carries the calf and dwells; [the other]... He has taken up his dwelling in the former ones and follows after the latter; as soon as they are born, he is within the young ones.
Pregnant, they bring forth without being impregnated...
The calf, lying beyond, now wanders as one with two mothers, though bound by no ties.
These are the ordinances of Mitra and Varuṇa...
The Hotṛ priest with two mothers, the sovereign in the assemblies, moves along the path of order; he dwells as the foundation.
Those of pleasant speech bring forth delightful offerings.
Like a hero fighting in the closest combat, everything approaching is seen turned toward him.
The inner intelligence moves within the cow’s stall.
The gray envoy stirs; the great one moves within with his light. Bearing wondrous forms, he looks upon us.
Viṣṇu, the protector, guards the supreme pasture, establishing his beloved abodes within the immortal realm. Agni knows all those worlds;
he... The twin sisters have fashioned their forms separately; of these two, one shines black, the other white.
When the two sisters, the dark one and the ruddy one, [meet]...
where the mother and the daughter, the two cows yielding plenty of milk, suckle together; I praise you within the seat of the Cosmic Order.
Licking the calf of another, she has lowed; in what world has the cow laid down her udder?
She, the *ilā*, swells with the milk of *ṛta*. She clothes herself in many-colored forms; standing erect, licking the three-year-old calf, she has ascended.

I, the knowing one, traverse the seat of *ṛta*. Like two footsteps set down by the wonder-worker, one of them is hidden within, the other is manifest. That path leads together, yet it goes in different directions.
Let the milch-cows come lowing—the barren ones, those that yield nectar, the restless, and those never milked.
Becoming ever new and youthful maidens, they flow forth.
When the bull bellows among others, he deposits his seed in another herd.
For he is the lord of the night, he is Bhaga, he is the King.
O people, let us now proclaim the hero’s possession of noble horses; O gods, they know him. Six teams, five by five, carry him.
The divine Tvaṣṭṛ, the impeller of all forms, has nourished all creatures and brought them forth in many ways;
he is the source of all these worlds.
He has joined together the two great, facing expanses of heaven and earth; both of them are filled with his wealth.
The hero is renowned as he acquires riches...
This earth, the sustainer of all, dwells near us; the king is established like a well-disposed friend, like heroes seated in the front for protection...
The plants and the waters ward off [evil] from you; O Indra, the earth bears wealth for you.
May we, your friends, be sharers in your favor. Neither the crafty nor the wise violate those first, firm decrees of the gods.
Neither the two worlds, free from malice, nor the mountains that stand firm have bowed down before the objects of knowledge.
One, moving not, sustains the six burdens; the cows have approached the highest *ṛta*. Three great ones stand above; two are hidden in secret, while one is visible.
The bull, possessing three bellies and all forms, has three udders and is manifoldly rich in offspring.

The three-fold, majestic one rules; he is the seed-bestowing bull of all eternal ones. May he, the knower of the path, be mindful of them in their presence; I have invoked the beloved name of the Ādityas.
Even the divine waters paused for him; though flowing separately, they encompassed him on every side.
The rivers have three abodes; the sage poets are threefold, and the mother of the three has sovereign sway over the sacrificial assemblies.
The three divine waters, observers of cosmic order (*ṛta*), are threefold; they rule as mistresses at the sacrifice from heaven thrice daily.
O Savitṛ, send us down thrice from heaven each day the choicest boons, and thrice during the course of the day.
O Bhaga, bestow threefold wealth and treasures; O Protector, grant us wisdom for our gain.
Three times from heaven Savitar impels his gifts; the two kings Mitra and Varuṇa are well-handed.
Even the waters and the two wide worlds beg for treasure at the impulse of Savitar.
Three times the highest, invincible luminaries shine; three heroes of the Asura rule as kings.
May the gods, observers of cosmic order (*ṛta*), vigorous and difficult to deceive, be present at the assembly of heaven three times a day.
He who discerns has found my inspired thought (*manīṣā*): a cow wandering at large, unguarded by a herdsman.

She who at once has yielded much for the sake of nourishment—Indra and Agni are her praisers. Indra and Pūṣan, the two bulls with skillful hands, like those pleased by heaven, have milked out the inexhaustible flow.
Since all the gods have taken delight in her, may I here obtain your favor, O Vasus.
The sisters who desire the bull’s power, paying homage, recognize the embryo within him. Like lowing cows toward their calf, they move toward him who bears great beauty.
Harnessing the pressing-stones with my thought at the sacrifice, I address the well-established heaven and earth.
These [flames] of yours, O Wondrous One, rise up for Manu, bringing many boons—visible and worthy of worship.

That honey-sweet and wise tongue of yours, O Agni, which speaks far-reaching words among the gods, with that bring all the worshipful ones here for our protection; seat them and let them drink the honeyed draughts.
O Agni, that brilliant, shimmering stream of yours which swells like a mountain torrent, O God—grant us that providence, O Jātavedas, O Vasu, and grant us a benevolence that extends to all people.
The Milch-cow of the Ancient One yields her desirable milk; the Son moves within the Dakṣiṇā.
The hymn of the Dawn, whose path is bright, has awakened the two Aśvins who carry the light.
They draw their well-yoked chariot toward you by the eternal law (*ṛta*); the sacred offerings rise up like ancestors.
O mighty ones, consume the food of the niggardly; we have prepared this protection for you—come hither!
O Wondrous Ones, with well-yoked horses and a well-rolling chariot, hear this hymn of Adre.
O Aśvins, why indeed do the ancient sages say that you are the ones most swift to return? Take heed of us;
come hither! Do all the people, along with the gods, call upon you, O Aśvins?
For these honeyed draughts, mixed with milk, have been offered to you two like friends at the first break of dawn.
O Aśvins, Maghavans, your praise resounds among the people across many realms.
Come hither by the paths traveled by the gods; O wonder-workers, here are your vessels of honeyed mead.
Ancient is your dwelling, auspicious is your friendship, O heroes; your wealth is in the house of Jahnu.
Renewing our auspicious friendships, may we together rejoice now in the sweetness of the honey, being one in spirit.
O Aśvins, you who are most skillful, young and in harmony with Vāyu and his teams of horses—
O Nāsatyas, you who are true, drinking the Soma after three days has passed, drink it without fail, O bounteous givers!
O Aśvins, abundant nourishments have gone forth around you, striving with unceasing songs of praise.
Your chariot, born of Truth and urged by the pressing-stones, traverses heaven and earth in an instant.
O Aśvins, this Soma, pressed with sweetness, is yours; come to our dwelling and drink it. Your chariot, assuming many forms, comes most readily to the prepared place of him who has pressed the juice.
Mitra, speaking, stirs men to action; Mitra has supported both the earth and the sky.
Mitra beholds the people with an unblinking eye; offer an oblation rich in ghee to Mitra.

May that mortal, O Mitra, be foremost and full of offerings who serves you, O Āditya, according to your law. He whom you protect is neither slain nor conquered; no distress reaches him, neither from near nor from afar.
Free from disease, rejoicing in the sacrificial food (*iḷā*), with measured steps upon the wide expanse of the earth,
and abiding by the ordinance of Āditya, may we remain in the benevolent favor of Mitra.
This Mitra, worthy of homage, most gracious, a king of noble power and a wise ordainer, has been born.
Of him we...

[we are the friends]. The great Āditya, who is to be approached with homage, who stirs the people, is most kind to the one who praises him. To that most praiseworthy Mitra, offer this acceptable oblation into the fire.
The aid of the god Mitra, the supporter of the people, is gainful; his splendor possesses most wonderful renown.
Mitra, who by his greatness has become coextensive with heaven, prevails over all.
With glories they have encompassed the earth; the five peoples have submitted to Mitra for his victorious might.
He sustains all the gods.
Mitra among the gods and among living beings, for the person who has strewn the sacred grass, he is the one whose vows are desired; he provides nourishment.
Here, here, O heroes, you who are eager, have come with your mind and kinship to these [offerings] through your wisdom.
By those wondrous powers (*māyā*) through which you, O sons of Sudhanvan, who were swift in your response, attained a share in the sacrifice;
by those skills (*śacī*) with which you fashioned the cups, and by that inspired thought (*dhī*) with which you brought forth the cow from the hide;
by that mind with which you wrought the two bay steeds (*harī*), through all that, O Ṛbhus, you attained divinity.
The Ṛbhus attained the friendship of Indra; the sons of Manu, skillful workers, exerted themselves.
The sons of Sudhanvan won immortality, having performed their labors with pious rites and through their well-executed work.
O Ṛbhus, you travel in one chariot with Indra at the pressed juice; then you become masters of all desires together with glory.
O priests, your well-performed deeds have no equal, nor do your heroic exploits, O R̥bhus, sons of Sudhanvan.
O Indra, together with the Vāja-possessing R̥bhus, pour down the pressed Soma from your hands;
impelled by devotion, O Maghavan, rejoice in the house of the donor along with the sons of Sudhanvan, the heroes.
O Indra, accompanied by the *Ṛbhus* and the *Vājas*, exhilarate yourself here for us at this libation with your power, O you who are praised by many!
These pastures have been prepared for you; the ordinances of the gods and the laws of men have been established according to their statutes.
O Indra, seeking booty with the vigorous *Ṛbhus*, come here to the praiseworthy hymn of the singer at this sacrifice.
With a hundred eager intentions, you come for the sake of the living man, with a thousand paths at the offering of the sacrifice.
O Dawn, rich in booty, wise one, accept the hymn of the singer, O bountiful lady!
Ancient yet youthful goddess, all-possessing, you move according to the sacred law, O you who have all desirable things.
O immortal goddess Dawn, shine forth, you who possess a radiant chariot and send forth pleasant truths.
Let the well-governed horses, broad-chested and golden-hued, bring you hither.
O Dawn, facing all beings, you stand upright as the banner of immortality.
Moving toward a common goal, turn hither like a wheel with your newest [chariot].
Like one gathering a fringe, the bounteous Dawn approaches, the mistress of the stall.
Generating light, the fortunate and wondrous one has spread from the ends of heaven to the earth.
Bring forth with reverence your hymn of praise toward the goddess Dawn as she shines forth.
The honey-bearer has fixed her splendor upward in heaven; she of lovely aspect has shone out through the luminous realms.
She, the observer of Truth, has been awakened by the hymns of heaven; the wealthy one has ascended to the two worlds in wondrous fashion.
O Agni, seeking desirable wealth, you go toward the approaching, radiant Dawn.
Seeking nourishment at the foundation of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), the Bull has entered the two great worlds, Heaven and Earth.
The great creative power (*māyā*) of Mitra and Varuṇa has spread its light in many places, like the moon.
These longings of ours, thinking of you both, have become as urgent for us as they were for one like you;
O Indra and Varuṇa, where is that glory of yours by which you bring wealth to your friends?
This man here, seeking riches, incessantly calls upon you both most frequently for protection.
O Indra and Varuṇa, being of one accord with the Maruts, hear my invocation from heaven and from earth.
O Indra and Varuṇa, may that wealth be ours; O Maruts, may there be for us riches consisting of all-heroic sons.
May the protectors guard us with their shelters; may Hotrā Bhāratī protect us with sacrificial gifts.
O Bṛhaspati, who belongs to all the gods, enjoy our oblations;
bestow treasures upon the donor. Worship the pure Bṛhaspati with hymns during the sacrifices.
He desires invincible power;
[I praise] Bṛhaspati, the bull of the people, who possesses every form and is invincible, the one to be chosen.
O Pūṣan, O unassailable god, this newest hymn of praise for you is being recited by us. Be pleased with that song of mine; favor my prayer as it strives for strength.
Like a suitor seeking a maiden,
may he who beholds all beings and surveys them together—
may that Pūṣan be our protector.
We meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he impel our thoughts. Seeking strength through the wisdom of Purandhi, we [meditate] upon the divine Savitṛ.
We pray for the bounty of Bhaga. Men, inspired by their devotion, worship the god Savitṛ with sacrifices and well-fashioned hymns. Driven by their thoughts, they pay him homage.
Soma goes forth, the knower of the way; he goes to the appointed place of the gods, to sit upon the womb of the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
Soma [bestows] for us bipeds and for our four-footed cattle.
May he provide us with food free from disease;
may Soma, increasing our lifespan and overcoming our adversaries, sit down upon his common seat.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, sprinkle our pastures with clarified butter; O you of noble wisdom, drench the regions with honey.
O you whose praise is wide, who increase through homage, you rule by the greatness of your skillful power.
With your longest [flames], O you of pure vows,
being praised by Jamadagni, sit in the womb of Cosmic Order.
